_comment: What a card says when the sky is not touching that area of a life.
Every one of the nine areas gets a card every day, so four or five of
them are usually these. That is the honest shape of a day: on a typical
morning only three or four parts of a chart have anything within orb, and
an app that shows nine equally confident cards is either widening its
orbs until everything counts or writing to fill a grid.
So these say the true thing instead, and the card underneath prints the
measurement that makes it true: which sign the sector runs in, which of
your planets live there, which are passing through today, and how far
outside orb the nearest angle is. A reader can check every one of those.
Four cases, chosen by the chart and not by a seed. The split matters: an
early version had one line for every area without a reading, which meant
four identical cards on a typical morning, and four cards saying one
sentence is the thing this grid exists to avoid.
near      a planet of yours sits here, and an angle is close but outside orb
still     a planet of yours sits here, and nothing is near it
visiting  nothing of yours here, but planets are crossing it today
empty     nothing of yours here, and nothing passing through
Three variants each, in the same [headline, body] shape readings.json
uses. Not for variety across days but for variety down the page: three
empty areas at once is ordinary, and the picker walks the list so no two
cards of the same kind on the same day can land on the same variant.
Every capitalised word must appear in the stop list in tools/validate-copy.mjs,
or the voice suite reads it as an invented proper noun.
Keep them declarative and keep them short. They are not consolation for
a missing reading, they are the reading. What they must never sound like
is an error message: the sentence says what is true of this area today,
in the same voice the reading cards use, and the sign clause from
signs.json supplies what the area is like the rest of the time.
depth is the third paragraph of the expanded card, one per kind. The
second paragraph comes from signs.json, so a quiet card still expands to
three paragraphs and two of the three are about this particular chart.

near: Something is lining up on this part of your chart and it has not arrived. The distance is printed below, in degrees. Nothing is being asked of you here today, which is worth knowing rather than filling in.
An angle is forming here and it is still short of the width that counts. Watch it rather than acting on it. The number below moves a little every day, so this is one to check tomorrow.
Something is approaching a planet of yours here and has not got there. Whatever you are feeling about this part of your life today is arriving from somewhere else on this page.
still: Yours, and nobody is asking anything of it.
Planets of yours sit here and nothing in the sky is at an angle to them today. This is what an ordinary day looks like from the inside, and most of your days are this one.
This part of your chart has your own planets standing in it and nothing is touching them. It is running on itself, which is usually when things here go well.
You have planets here and the sky is addressing none of them today. What sits here is listed below, and it is doing its own work without supervision.
visiting: The sign is doing the talking here.
Planets are crossing this part of your chart today and none of yours is standing here to meet them, so the sign is what this area is running on.
Traffic, and none of it is yours.
Something is passing through this sector today and your chart left it unoccupied, so what happens here is a matter of the sign rather than of the traffic.
Read this one off the sign.
What is crossing is listed below. It is making an angle to none of your own points, because none of them live here, so the sign is the whole of the reading.
empty: This one runs on its sign alone.
No planet of yours sits here and none is crossing today, which leaves the sign it was born under as the whole of what this area is.
Quiet by construction, not by accident.
Twelve sectors and ten planets leaves several parts of every chart unoccupied for life. This is one of them, and the sign on it is what it has.
This part of the chart is unoccupied, so it does not change much. What it is like, it is like permanently, and the sign below says which.

depth.near: An angle only counts inside its orb, and the orb is not a formality. Outside that width, two bodies are simply two bodies standing at an angle nobody reads. This one is close enough to be worth looking at again tomorrow.
depth.still: A part of a chart with planets in it and nothing touching them is having an ordinary day, which most days are. Nothing here is being pushed or helped, and that is worth knowing before you go looking for a reason for how the day is going.
depth.visiting: A body passing through a sector is not the same as a body making an angle to something in it. This is traffic through an empty room: real, measurable, and touching nothing of yours, because there is nothing of yours here to touch.
depth.empty: Ten bodies cannot occupy twelve sectors, so several parts of every chart stand empty for life. That is not a fault in the chart. It means this area is read from the sign on it and from whatever happens to be crossing, rather than from anything of your own standing here.
